clinical_knowledge.topic: Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease (AERD / Samter's Triad) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease (AERD / Samter's Triad) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management is strict avoidance of aspirin and other COX-1-inhibiting NSAIDs, with aspirin desensitization under specialist supervision as a long-term option, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: nasal polyps, chronic asthma, and acute wheezing attack after taking aspirin or ibuprofen
Key HPI features: 48M with chronic rhinosinusitis and nasal polyps presenting with acute severe bronchospasm and facial flushing within 60 minutes of taking ibuprofen for headache.
Objective/Exam findings: Diffuse expiratory wheeze and facial flushing during the acute reaction; nasal exam shows polyposis; no urticaria.
Relevant background/PMH: Asthma; chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease (AERD / Samter's Triad).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to True IgE-mediated NSAID allergy (urticaria/anaphylaxis type) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe bronchospasm requiring emergency treatment after NSAID use.
management_principles: Strictly avoid aspirin and other COX-1-inhibiting NSAIDs; consider aspirin desensitization under specialist supervision for long-term control
Refer to specialty team and provide comprehensive patient counseling
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease AERD Samter Triad: nasal polyps, chronic asthma, and acute wheezing attack after taking aspirin or ibuprofen. 48M with chronic rhinosinusitis and nasal polyps presenting with acute severe bronchospasm and facial flushing within 60 minutes of taking ibuprofen for headache.
reference_soap.objective: Diffuse expiratory wheeze and facial flushing during the acute reaction; nasal exam shows polyposis; no urticaria.
reference_soap.assessment: Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease (AERD / Samter's Triad) with acute NSAID-induced bronchospasm.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Treat the acute bronchospasm with standard asthma exacerbation therapy (bronchodilators, systemic corticosteroids as needed); do not give aspirin or any NSAID acutely. 2. Strictly avoid aspirin and other COX-1-inhibiting NSAIDs going forward (acetaminophen and COX-2-selective agents are generally better tolerated). 3. Refer to allergy/immunology for consideration of supervised aspirin desensitization and to ENT for polyp management.

teaching.one_liner: The triad of asthma, nasal polyps, and acute bronchospasm within an hour of taking aspirin or any NSAID — a pseudoallergic COX-1 reaction, not true IgE allergy.
differentials: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps alone
red_flags: Severe bronchospasm requiring emergency treatment after NSAID use
Facial flushing with breathing difficulty — can mimic anaphylaxis
